This Week: Content, Thought Leadership & the Narrative Advantage

July 7, 2026

Happy Monday! This week we're diving into Unit 6: Content, Thought Leadership, and the Narrative Advantage — arguably the most practically useful unit in the curriculum for day-to-day PMM work.

📚 This Week's Focus: Unit 6

Unit 6 of 8

Content, Thought Leadership & the Narrative Advantage

Why 80% of B2B content fails to generate pipeline — and how AI changes both the problem and the solution.

What you'll learn:

  • The 80/20 pattern: why most content gets ignored
  • Performative vs. genuine thought leadership
  • GEO: The Agent as Reader — how AI consumes content differently
  • The Three-Layer Content Operating Model
  • Practical playbook for AI-augmented content creation

Why this matters now: With Cloudflare defaulting to blocking AI crawlers starting September 15, and tools like Profound's Aim turning GEO into an operational system, understanding how to create content that serves both human readers AND AI systems is no longer optional.

📰 News of the Week

Big week for agentic infrastructure. The pattern is clear: AI isn't just a feature anymore — it's becoming the operating system.

1. Microsoft Launches Frontier Co. ($2.5B, 6,000 Engineers)

A dedicated subsidiary to embed AI inside client operations. AI adoption is now a service, not just a product.

2. Zoom Acquires Common Room

Video + conversation intelligence + buyer signals in one GTM stack. The data layer just consolidated.

3. Gartner: $234B in SaaS at Risk from Agentic AI

"Agentic arbitrage" — when agents complete tasks across apps without users touching them — will reshape enterprise software.

4. Profound Launches "Aim" — Agentic GEO

Finally: GEO as an operational system, not just an audit. Monitors AI visibility, creates briefs, routes work to agents.

5. Klaviyo Ships Multi-Agent Marketing Teams

Agents that coordinate with each other — one evaluates segments, another builds campaigns, a third adjusts flows.
